name: AlphaRAR.eradeAlgorithm
doc: The **ERADE 2025** aRTS design as an `Algorithm` (Example 3.2 of the paper).

binders.name: hTnn
binders.type: ∀ (z : 𝓐 → ℝ) (k : 𝓐), 0 ≤ T z k

binders.name: hTsum
binders.type: ∀ (z : 𝓐 → ℝ), ∑ k, T z k = 1

statement.conclusion: Learning.Algorithm Unit 𝓐 ℝ

code:
/-- The **ERADE 2025** aRTS design as an `Algorithm` (Example 3.2 of the paper). -/
noncomputable def eradeAlgorithm (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hT : Continuous T)
    (hTnn : ∀ z k, 0 ≤ T z k) (hTsum : ∀ z, ∑ k, T z k = 1) {α : ℝ}
    (hα : α ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : Algorithm Unit 𝓐 ℝ :=
  aRTSAlgorithmOfProb (eradeProb θ₀ T α) (fun n k ↦ measurable_eradeProb θ₀ hT α n k)
    (fun n h a ↦ eradeProb_nonneg θ₀ hTnn hα n h a) (fun n h ↦ eradeProb_sum θ₀ hTsum α n h)

specifiedBy.comment: the only thing the packaged algorithm has to be: a member of the aRTS family, so that every result about that family applies to it

name: AlphaRAR.eradeProb
doc:
The **ERADE 2025** design's probability vector: over-sampled arms are throttled to `α ρ̂_k`,
arms at their target keep `ρ̂_k`, and each under-sampled arm receives `ρ̂_k` plus an equal share
`(1-α)(∑_{over} ρ̂_j)/|under|` of the mass freed from the over-sampled arms.

statement.conclusion: ℝ
statement.value:
if histTarget θ₀ T k n h < histProp n h k then α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h
else
  if histProp n h k < histTarget θ₀ T k n h then
    histTarget θ₀ T k n h +
      (1 - α) *
        ((∑ j, if histTarget θ₀ T j n h < histProp n h j then histTarget θ₀ T j n h else 0) /
          ∑ j, if histProp n h j < histTarget θ₀ T j n h then 1 else 0)
  else histTarget θ₀ T k n h

code:
/-- The **ERADE 2025** design's probability vector: over-sampled arms are throttled to `α ρ̂_k`,
arms at their target keep `ρ̂_k`, and each under-sampled arm receives `ρ̂_k` plus an equal share
`(1-α)(∑_{over} ρ̂_j)/|under|` of the mass freed from the over-sampled arms. -/
noncomputable def eradeProb (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) (T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ) (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐) : ℝ :=
  letI : DecidablePred fun j : 𝓐 ↦ histTarget θ₀ T j n h < histProp n h j := fun _ ↦ Classical.dec _
  letI : DecidablePred fun j : 𝓐 ↦ histProp n h j < histTarget θ₀ T j n h := fun _ ↦ Classical.dec _
  if histTarget θ₀ T k n h < histProp n h k then α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h
  else if histProp n h k < histTarget θ₀ T k n h then
    histTarget θ₀ T k n h + (1 - α)
      * ((∑ j, if histTarget θ₀ T j n h < histProp n h j then histTarget θ₀ T j n h else 0)
        / ∑ j, if histProp n h j < histTarget θ₀ T j n h then (1 : ℝ) else 0)
  else histTarget θ₀ T k n h

specifiedBy.comment: the redistribution is exactly mass-preserving: the `(1-α)` taken from the over-sampled arms is precisely what the equal shares hand to the under-sampled ones, and the arms sitting at their target are left alone
the design's membership in the aRTS family, and it confirms the branch condition `ρ̂_k < N_k/n` is the same over-sampling test `IsARTS` uses

name: AlphaRAR.probVecKernel
doc:
The kernel `x ↦ ∑ₐ p(x,a) δₐ` built from a measurable probability-vector function
`p : X → 𝓐 → ℝ` on a finite action space `𝓐`. When `p x` is a genuine probability vector
(nonnegative, summing to `1`) this is a Markov kernel (`probVecKernel.isMarkovKernel`).

binders.name: hp
binders.type: ∀ (a : 𝓐), Measurable fun x => p x a

statement.conclusion: ProbabilityTheory.Kernel X 𝓐
statement.value: { toFun := fun x => ∑ a, ENNReal.ofReal (p x a) • MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac a, measurable' := ⋯ }

code:
/-- The kernel `x ↦ ∑ₐ p(x,a) δₐ` built from a measurable probability-vector function
`p : X → 𝓐 → ℝ` on a finite action space `𝓐`. When `p x` is a genuine probability vector
(nonnegative, summing to `1`) this is a Markov kernel (`probVecKernel.isMarkovKernel`). -/
noncomputable def probVecKernel (p : X → 𝓐 → ℝ) (hp : ∀ a, Measurable fun x ↦ p x a) :
    Kernel X 𝓐 where
  toFun x := ∑ a, ENNReal.ofReal (p x a) • Measure.dirac a
  measurable' := by
    refine Measure.measurable_of_measurable_coe _ fun s hs ↦ ?_
    simp only [Measure.finsetSum_apply, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    exact Finset.measurable_sum _ fun a _ ↦ (hp a).ennreal_ofReal.mul_const _

specifiedBy.comment: the kernel really samples from `p`: the mass it assigns to each arm is that arm's coordinate, with the `ℝ≥0∞` round-trip doing nothing on nonnegative inputs
the construction is total — it accepts any measurable `p` — but is a *Markov* kernel exactly under the simplex conditions, which is why every design below has to prove its `_nonneg` and `_sum` lemmas

name: AlphaRAR.distanceProb
doc:
The **distance-based** design's probability vector: `p_k = α ρ̂_k + (1-α) δ_k / (∑_i δ_i)` with
under-sampling deficit `δ_k = max(0, ρ̂_k - N_k/(n+1))`, degenerating to `ρ̂_k` when `∑ δ = 0`.

statement.conclusion: ℝ
statement.value:
if ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i) = 0 then histTarget θ₀ T k n h
else
  α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h +
    (1 - α) *
      (max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T k n h - histProp n h k) /
        ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i))

code:
/-- The **distance-based** design's probability vector: `p_k = α ρ̂_k + (1-α) δ_k / (∑_i δ_i)` with
under-sampling deficit `δ_k = max(0, ρ̂_k - N_k/(n+1))`, degenerating to `ρ̂_k` when `∑ δ = 0`. -/
noncomputable def distanceProb (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) (T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ) (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐) : ℝ :=
  haveI : Decidable (∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i) = 0) := Classical.dec _
  if ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i) = 0 then histTarget θ₀ T k n h
  else α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h
    + (1 - α) * (max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T k n h - histProp n h k)
      / ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i))

specifiedBy.comment: with `distanceProb_nonneg`, the design is a genuine randomization rule; in particular the degenerate branch `∑ δ = 0` was given the right fallback value `ρ̂_k`, which is the one choice that keeps the total mass at `1`
the design's membership in the aRTS family: the `max 0 (·)` deficit is what makes an over-sampled arm receive none of the exploration mass, so its probability collapses to the throttled `α ρ̂_k`

name: AlphaRAR.eradeProb_nonneg
doc: Each ERADE probability is nonnegative.

binders.name: hTnn
binders.type: ∀ (z : 𝓐 → ℝ) (k : 𝓐), 0 ≤ T z k

statement.conclusion: 0 ≤ eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k

code:
/-- Each ERADE probability is nonnegative. -/
lemma eradeProb_nonneg (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hTnn : ∀ z k, 0 ≤ T z k)
    {α : ℝ} (hα : α ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐) :
    0 ≤ eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k
proof:
:= by
  have hρnn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ histTarget θ₀ T i n h := fun i ↦ by simp only [histTarget]; exact hTnn _ _
  simp only [eradeProb]
  split_ifs with h1 h2
  · exact mul_nonneg hα.1 (hρnn k)
  · refine add_nonneg (hρnn k) (mul_nonneg (by linarith [hα.2]) (div_nonneg ?_ ?_))
    · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun j _ ↦ by split_ifs; exacts [hρnn j, le_refl 0]
    · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun j _ ↦ by split_ifs; exacts [zero_le_one, le_refl 0]
  · exact hρnn k

/-- **The ERADE 2025 design belongs to the aRTS family.** -/

family, so that every result about that family applies to it"]
lemma erade_isARTS (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hT : Continuous T)
    (hTnn : ∀ z k, 0 ≤ T z k) (hTsum : ∀ z, ∑ k, T z k = 1) {α : ℝ}

name: AlphaRAR.measurable_eradeProb
doc: Measurability of the ERADE probability in the history.

statement.conclusion: Measurable fun h => eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k

code:
/-- Measurability of the ERADE probability in the history. -/
lemma measurable_eradeProb (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hT : Continuous T) (α : ℝ)
    (n : ℕ) (k : 𝓐) : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k
proof:
:= by
  classical
  have hρ : ∀ i, Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ histTarget θ₀ T i n h :=
    fun i ↦ measurable_histTarget θ₀ hT i n
  have hq : ∀ i, Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ histProp n h i :=
    fun i ↦ measurable_histProp i n
  have hA : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦
      ∑ j, if histTarget θ₀ T j n h < histProp n h j then histTarget θ₀ T j n h else 0 :=
    Finset.measurable_sum _ fun j _ ↦
      Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (hρ j) (hq j)) (hρ j) measurable_const
  have hTc : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦
      ∑ j, if histProp n h j < histTarget θ₀ T j n h then (1 : ℝ) else 0 :=
    Finset.measurable_sum _ fun j _ ↦
      Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (hq j) (hρ j)) measurable_const measurable_const
  simp only [eradeProb]
  refine Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (hρ k) (hq k)) (measurable_const.mul (hρ k)) ?_
  exact Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (hq k) (hρ k))
    ((hρ k).add (measurable_const.mul (hA.div hTc))) (hρ k)

@[specifies distanceProb "with `distanceProb_nonneg`, the design is a genuine randomization rule; \

    (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) : ∑ k, distanceProb θ₀ T α n h k = 1

  simp only [distanceProb]
  split_ifs with hS

      ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_div, div_self hS, mul_one]
    ring

specifies.comment: with `distanceProb_nonneg`, the design is a genuine randomization rule; in particular the degenerate branch `∑ δ = 0` was given the right fallback value `ρ̂_k`, which is the one choice that keeps the total mass at `1`

name: AlphaRAR.aRTSAlgorithmOfProb
doc:
The `Algorithm` whose policy at each step draws the next arm from the history-dependent
probability vector `p n h` (the observation is trivial and plays no role). Requires `p n h` to be
measurable in `h` and a probability vector.

binders.name: p
binders.type: (n : ℕ) → Learning.Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n → 𝓐 → ℝ

binders.name: hp
binders.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : 𝓐), Measurable fun h => p n h a

binders.name: hnn
binders.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Learning.Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (a : 𝓐), 0 ≤ p n h a

binders.name: hsum
binders.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Learning.Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n), ∑ a, p n h a = 1

statement.conclusion: Learning.Algorithm Unit 𝓐 ℝ
statement.value: { policy := fun n => probVecKernel (fun x => p n x.1) ⋯, isMarkovKernel_policy := ⋯ }

code:
/-- The `Algorithm` whose policy at each step draws the next arm from the history-dependent
probability vector `p n h` (the observation is trivial and plays no role). Requires `p n h` to be
measurable in `h` and a probability vector. -/
noncomputable def aRTSAlgorithmOfProb (p : (n : ℕ) → Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n → 𝓐 → ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ n a, Measurable fun h ↦ p n h a) (hnn : ∀ n h a, 0 ≤ p n h a)
    (hsum : ∀ n h, ∑ a, p n h a = 1) : Algorithm Unit 𝓐 ℝ where
  policy n := probVecKernel (fun x : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n × Unit ↦ p n x.1)
    (fun a ↦ (hp n a).comp measurable_fst)
  isMarkovKernel_policy n :=
    probVecKernel.isMarkovKernel _ _ (fun x ↦ hnn n x.1) (fun x ↦ hsum n x.1)

specifiedBy.comment: the packaging is faithful: the algorithm's policy assigns arm `k` exactly the mass `p n h k`, so a throttle proved for the probability vector holds verbatim for the algorithm

name: AlphaRAR.sum_histProp
doc: The allocation proportions sum to `1` on a nonempty history.

statement.conclusion: ∑ k, histProp n h k = 1

code:
/-- The allocation proportions sum to `1` on a nonempty history. -/
@[specifies histProp "the denominator `n` is the right one: it is exactly the number of patients \
seen in a history of `n` rounds, so the proportions form a probability vector and are \
directly comparable with the simplex-valued target `histTarget`"]
lemma sum_histProp {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) : ∑ k, histProp n h k = 1
proof:
:= by
  simp only [histProp, ← Finset.sum_div]
  rw [show (∑ k, (pullCount' n h k : ℝ)) = (n : ℝ) by rw [← Nat.cast_sum, sum_pullCount']]
  rw [div_self (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr hn)]

specifies.comment: the denominator `n` is the right one: it is exactly the number of patients seen in a history of `n` rounds, so the proportions form a probability vector and are directly comparable with the simplex-valued target `histTarget`

name: AlphaRAR.measurable_dTrackingProb
doc: Measurability of the D-Tracking probability in the history.

statement.conclusion: Measurable fun h => dTrackingProb θ₀ T α n h k

code:
/-- Measurability of the D-Tracking probability in the history. -/
lemma measurable_dTrackingProb (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hT : Continuous T) (α : ℝ)
    (n : ℕ) (k : 𝓐) : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ dTrackingProb θ₀ T α n h k
proof:
:= by
  have hρ : ∀ i, Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ histTarget θ₀ T i n h :=
    fun i ↦ measurable_histTarget θ₀ hT i n
  have hdef : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ (fun a ↦ dtDeficit θ₀ T n h a) := by
    refine Measurable.of_eval fun a ↦ ?_
    simp only [dtDeficit]
    exact (measurable_const.mul (hρ a)).sub
      (measurable_from_top.comp (measurable_pullCount' n a))
  have hargmax : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦
      _root_.argmax (fun a ↦ dtDeficit θ₀ T n h a) :=
    measurable_argmax.comp hdef
  simp only [dTrackingProb]
  refine (measurable_const.mul (hρ k)).add (measurable_const.mul ?_)
  exact Measurable.ite (measurableSet_eq_fun measurable_const hargmax) measurable_const
    measurable_const

name: AlphaRAR.distanceProb_nonneg
doc: Each distance-based probability is nonnegative.

binders.name: hTnn
binders.type: ∀ (z : 𝓐 → ℝ) (k : 𝓐), 0 ≤ T z k

statement.conclusion: 0 ≤ distanceProb θ₀ T α n h k

code:
/-- Each distance-based probability is nonnegative. -/
lemma distanceProb_nonneg (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hTnn : ∀ z k, 0 ≤ T z k)
    {α : ℝ} (hα : α ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐) :
    0 ≤ distanceProb θ₀ T α n h k
proof:
:= by
  have hρnn : 0 ≤ histTarget θ₀ T k n h := by simp only [histTarget]; exact hTnn _ _
  have hSnn : 0 ≤ ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i) :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ ↦ le_max_left _ _
  simp only [distanceProb]
  split_ifs with hS
  · exact hρnn
  · have h1 : 0 ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h := mul_nonneg hα.1 hρnn
    have h2 : 0 ≤ (1 - α) * (max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T k n h - histProp n h k)
        / ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i)) :=
      mul_nonneg (by linarith [hα.2]) (div_nonneg (le_max_left _ _) hSnn)
    linarith

name: AlphaRAR.distanceProb_throttle
doc:
**Distance-based is aRTS**: when arm `k` is over-sampled its deficit vanishes, forcing
`p_k = α ρ̂_k`; the mixing normaliser is positive because some *other* arm is then under-sampled
(the deficits sum to `0` and are nonnegative after the `max`).

binders.name: hTsum
binders.type: ∀ (z : 𝓐 → ℝ), ∑ k, T z k = 1

binders.name: hover
binders.type: ↑n * histTarget θ₀ T k n h < ↑(Learning.pullCount' n h k)

statement.conclusion: distanceProb θ₀ T α n h k ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h

code:
/-- **Distance-based is aRTS**: when arm `k` is over-sampled its deficit vanishes, forcing
`p_k = α ρ̂_k`; the mixing normaliser is positive because some *other* arm is then under-sampled
(the deficits sum to `0` and are nonnegative after the `max`). -/
@[specifies distanceProb "the design's membership in the aRTS family: the `max 0 (·)` deficit is \
what makes an over-sampled arm receive none of the exploration mass, so its probability collapses \
to the throttled `α ρ̂_k`"]
lemma distanceProb_throttle (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hTsum : ∀ z, ∑ k, T z k = 1)
    (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐)
    (hover : (n : ℝ) * histTarget θ₀ T k n h < (pullCount' n h k : ℝ)) :
    distanceProb θ₀ T α n h k ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h
proof:
:= by
  have hn : n ≠ 0 := ne_zero_of_over_sampled hover
  have hnp : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := Nat.cast_pos.mpr (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
  have hlt : histTarget θ₀ T k n h < histProp n h k := by
    rw [histProp, lt_div_iff₀ hnp]; linarith [hover]
  have hδk : max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T k n h - histProp n h k) = 0 := by
    rw [max_eq_left]; linarith
  have hsum0 : ∑ i, (histProp n h i - histTarget θ₀ T i n h) = 0 := by
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, sum_histProp hn, sum_histTarget θ₀ hTsum]; ring
  have hSpos : 0 < ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i) := by
    obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ : ∃ j ∈ Finset.univ, histProp n h j - histTarget θ₀ T j n h < 0 := by
      by_contra hcon
      push Not at hcon
      have hpos : 0 < ∑ i, (histProp n h i - histTarget θ₀ T i n h) :=
        Finset.sum_pos' (fun i _ ↦ hcon i (Finset.mem_univ i))
          ⟨k, Finset.mem_univ k, by linarith⟩
      linarith
    refine Finset.sum_pos' (fun i _ ↦ le_max_left _ _) ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ j, ?_⟩
    rw [lt_max_iff]; right; linarith
  refine le_of_eq ?_
  simp only [distanceProb, ite_eq_right hSpos.ne', hδk, zero_div, mul_zero, add_zero]

specifies.comment: the design's membership in the aRTS family: the `max 0 (·)` deficit is what makes an over-sampled arm receive none of the exploration mass, so its probability collapses to the throttled `α ρ̂_k`

code:
/-- The mass the kernel puts on a single arm `k` is `p x k` (for `p x k ≥ 0`). -/
@[specifies probVecKernel "the kernel really samples from `p`: the mass it assigns to each arm is \
that arm's coordinate, with the `ℝ≥0∞` round-trip doing nothing on nonnegative inputs"]
lemma probVecKernel_apply_singleton (p : X → 𝓐 → ℝ) (hp : ∀ a, Measurable fun x ↦ p x a) (x : X)
    (k : 𝓐) (hnn : 0 ≤ p x k) : (probVecKernel p hp x {k}).toReal = p x k
proof:
:= by
  rw [probVecKernel_apply, Measure.finsetSum_apply]
  have hzero : ∀ a ∈ (univ : Finset 𝓐), a ≠ k →
      (ENNReal.ofReal (p x a) • Measure.dirac a) {k} = 0 := by
    intro a _ hak
    rw [Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Measure.dirac_apply' _ (measurableSet_singleton k),
      Set.indicator_of_notMem (by simpa using hak), mul_zero]
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem k (mem_univ k) hzero, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    Measure.dirac_apply' k (measurableSet_singleton k),
    Set.indicator_of_mem (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mpr rfl), Pi.one_apply, mul_one,
    ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hnn]

specifies.comment: the kernel really samples from `p`: the mass it assigns to each arm is that arm's coordinate, with the `ℝ≥0∞` round-trip doing nothing on nonnegative inputs

doc: Measurability of the distance-based probability in the history.

statement.conclusion: Measurable fun h => distanceProb θ₀ T α n h k

code:
/-- Measurability of the distance-based probability in the history. -/
lemma measurable_distanceProb (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hT : Continuous T) (α : ℝ)
    (n : ℕ) (k : 𝓐) : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ distanceProb θ₀ T α n h k
proof:
:= by
  classical
  have hρ : ∀ i, Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦ histTarget θ₀ T i n h :=
    fun i ↦ measurable_histTarget θ₀ hT i n
  have hδ : ∀ i, Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦
      max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i) :=
    fun i ↦ measurable_const.max ((hρ i).sub (measurable_histProp i n))
  have hS : Measurable fun h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n ↦
      ∑ i, max 0 (histTarget θ₀ T i n h - histProp n h i) := Finset.measurable_sum _ fun i _ ↦ hδ i
  simp only [distanceProb]
  refine Measurable.ite (measurableSet_eq_fun hS measurable_const) (hρ k) ?_
  exact ((measurable_const.mul (hρ k)).add
    (measurable_const.mul ((hδ k).div hS)))

name: AlphaRAR.dTrackingProb_throttle
doc:
**Interpolated D-Tracking is aRTS**: an over-sampled arm has negative deficit, while the maximal
deficit is `≥ 0` (deficits sum to `0`), so an over-sampled arm is never the favoured `k⋆` and
receives exactly `p_k = α ρ̂_k`.

binders.type: ∀ (z : 𝓐 → ℝ), ∑ k, T z k = 1

statement.conclusion: dTrackingProb θ₀ T α n h k ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h

code:
/-- **Interpolated D-Tracking is aRTS**: an over-sampled arm has negative deficit, while the maximal
deficit is `≥ 0` (deficits sum to `0`), so an over-sampled arm is never the favoured `k⋆` and
receives exactly `p_k = α ρ̂_k`. -/
@[specifies dTrackingProb "the design's membership in the aRTS family; it also shows the `argmax` \
tie-breaking is irrelevant, since *no* over-sampled arm can be selected however ties are resolved"]
lemma dTrackingProb_throttle (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hTsum : ∀ z, ∑ k, T z k = 1)
    (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐)
    (hover : (n : ℝ) * histTarget θ₀ T k n h < (pullCount' n h k : ℝ)) :
    dTrackingProb θ₀ T α n h k ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h
proof:
:= by
  set d := fun a ↦ dtDeficit θ₀ T n h a with hddef
  have hk_neg : d k < 0 := by simp only [hddef, dtDeficit]; linarith
  -- The deficits sum to `0`, so the maximal deficit is `≥ 0`.
  have hdsum : ∑ a, d a = 0 := by rw [hddef]; exact sum_dtDeficit θ₀ hTsum n h
  have hMnn : 0 ≤ d (_root_.argmax d) := by
    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, 0 ≤ d j := by
      by_contra hcon
      push Not at hcon
      exact absurd hdsum (Finset.sum_neg (fun i _ ↦ hcon i) univ_nonempty).ne
    exact le_trans hj (isMaxOn_argmax d j)
  have hne : k ≠ _root_.argmax d := fun heq ↦ absurd (heq ▸ hk_neg) (not_lt.mpr hMnn)
  refine le_of_eq ?_
  simp only [dTrackingProb, ← hddef, ite_eq_right hne, mul_zero, add_zero]

specifies.comment: the design's membership in the aRTS family; it also shows the `argmax` tie-breaking is irrelevant, since *no* over-sampled arm can be selected however ties are resolved

name: AlphaRAR.eradeProb_sum
doc: **ERADE 2025 is a valid probability vector.**

binders.name: hTsum
binders.type: ∀ (z : 𝓐 → ℝ), ∑ k, T z k = 1

statement.conclusion: ∑ k, eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k = 1

code:
/-- **ERADE 2025 is a valid probability vector.** -/
@[specifies eradeProb "the redistribution is exactly mass-preserving: the `(1-α)` taken from the \
over-sampled arms is precisely what the equal shares hand to the under-sampled ones, and the arms \
sitting at their target are left alone"]
lemma eradeProb_sum (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (hTsum : ∀ z, ∑ k, T z k = 1)
    (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) : ∑ k, eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k = 1
proof:
:= by
  classical
  set A := ∑ j, if histTarget θ₀ T j n h < histProp n h j then histTarget θ₀ T j n h else 0
    with hAdef
  set Tc := ∑ j, if histProp n h j < histTarget θ₀ T j n h then (1 : ℝ) else 0 with hTcdef
  have hpk : ∀ k, eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k = histTarget θ₀ T k n h
      + (if histTarget θ₀ T k n h < histProp n h k then (α - 1) * histTarget θ₀ T k n h else 0)
      + (if histProp n h k < histTarget θ₀ T k n h then (1 - α) * A / Tc else 0) := by
    intro k
    simp only [eradeProb, ← hAdef, ← hTcdef]
    by_cases hover : histTarget θ₀ T k n h < histProp n h k
    · rw [ite_eq_left hover, ite_eq_left hover, ite_eq_right (not_lt.mpr hover.le)]; ring
    · rw [ite_eq_right hover, ite_eq_right hover]
      by_cases hunder : histProp n h k < histTarget θ₀ T k n h
      · rw [ite_eq_left hunder, ite_eq_left hunder]; ring
      · rw [ite_eq_right hunder, ite_eq_right hunder]; ring
  have hover_sum :
      (∑ k, if histTarget θ₀ T k n h < histProp n h k then (α - 1) * histTarget θ₀ T k n h else 0)
        = (α - 1) * A := by
    rw [hAdef, Finset.mul_sum]; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ ↦ by split_ifs <;> ring
  have hunder_sum :
      (∑ k, if histProp n h k < histTarget θ₀ T k n h then (1 - α) * A / Tc else 0)
        = Tc * ((1 - α) * A / Tc) := by
    rw [hTcdef, Finset.sum_mul]; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ ↦ by split_ifs <;> ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k _ ↦ hpk k), Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    hover_sum, hunder_sum, sum_histTarget θ₀ hTsum n h]
  by_cases hTc0 : Tc = 0
  · -- No arm is under-sampled, so (by mass conservation) no arm is over-sampled and `A = 0`.
    have hA0 : A = 0 := by
      have hnn : ∀ i ∈ (univ : Finset 𝓐),
          (0 : ℝ) ≤ if histProp n h i < histTarget θ₀ T i n h then (1 : ℝ) else 0 :=
        fun i _ ↦ by split_ifs <;> norm_num
      have hTcsum : (∑ j, if histProp n h j < histTarget θ₀ T j n h then (1 : ℝ) else 0) = 0 := by
        rw [← hTcdef]; exact hTc0
      have hall := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg hnn).mp hTcsum
      have hge : ∀ j, histTarget θ₀ T j n h ≤ histProp n h j := by
        intro j
        by_contra hj
        have := hall j (mem_univ j)
        rw [ite_eq_left (not_le.mp hj)] at this
        exact one_ne_zero this
      have hzero : ∑ j, (histProp n h j - histTarget θ₀ T j n h) = 0 := by
        rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, sum_histTarget θ₀ hTsum]
        have hge' : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j, histProp n h j := by
          rw [← sum_histTarget θ₀ hTsum n h]
          exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ ↦ hge j
        linarith [sum_histProp_le n h]
      have heq : ∀ j, histProp n h j = histTarget θ₀ T j n h := by
        intro j
        have hnn' : ∀ i ∈ (univ : Finset 𝓐),
            (0 : ℝ) ≤ histProp n h i - histTarget θ₀ T i n h := fun i _ ↦ by linarith [hge i]
        linarith [(Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg hnn').mp hzero j (mem_univ j)]
      rw [hAdef]
      exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun j _ ↦ ite_eq_right (by rw [heq j]; exact lt_irrefl _)
    rw [hTc0, hA0]; ring
  · rw [mul_comm Tc, div_mul_cancel₀ _ hTc0]; ring

specifies.comment: the redistribution is exactly mass-preserving: the `(1-α)` taken from the over-sampled arms is precisely what the equal shares hand to the under-sampled ones, and the arms sitting at their target are left alone

doc: **ERADE 2025 is aRTS**: an over-sampled arm gets exactly `p_k = α ρ̂_k`.

code:
/-- **ERADE 2025 is aRTS**: an over-sampled arm gets exactly `p_k = α ρ̂_k`. -/
@[specifies eradeProb "the design's membership in the aRTS family, and it confirms the branch \
condition `ρ̂_k < N_k/n` is the same over-sampling test `IsARTS` uses"]
lemma eradeProb_throttle (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) {T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ} (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n)
    (k : 𝓐) (hover : (n : ℝ) * histTarget θ₀ T k n h < (pullCount' n h k : ℝ)) :
    eradeProb θ₀ T α n h k ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h
proof:
:= by
  have hnp : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) :=
    Nat.cast_pos.mpr (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (ne_zero_of_over_sampled hover))
  have hlt : histTarget θ₀ T k n h < histProp n h k := by
    rw [histProp, lt_div_iff₀ hnp]; linarith
  refine le_of_eq ?_
  simp only [eradeProb, ite_eq_left hlt]

specifies.comment: the design's membership in the aRTS family, and it confirms the branch condition `ρ̂_k < N_k/n` is the same over-sampling test `IsARTS` uses

name: AlphaRAR.aRTSAlgorithmOfProb_isARTS
doc:
**The throttle characterisation of the aRTS family.** If the design's probability vector `p`
throttles every over-sampled arm --- `n ρ̂_k < N_k ⟹ p_k ≤ α ρ̂_k` --- then the algorithm it
builds belongs to the aRTS family (`IsARTS`). This reduces verifying `IsARTS` for a concrete design
to the pure arithmetic of its throttle inequality (`probVecKernel_apply_singleton` identifies the
policy mass on arm `k` with `p n h k`).

binders.name: p
binders.type: (n : ℕ) → Learning.Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n → 𝓐 → ℝ

binders.name: hp
binders.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : 𝓐), Measurable fun h => p n h a

binders.name: hnn
binders.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Learning.Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (a : 𝓐), 0 ≤ p n h a

binders.name: hsum
binders.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Learning.Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n), ∑ a, p n h a = 1

binders.name: hthrottle
binders.type:
∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Learning.Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐),
  ↑n * histTarget θ₀ T k n h < ↑(Learning.pullCount' n h k) → p n h k ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h

statement.conclusion: IsARTS (aRTSAlgorithmOfProb p hp hnn hsum) θ₀ T α

code:
/-- **The throttle characterisation of the aRTS family.** If the design's probability vector `p`
throttles every over-sampled arm --- `n ρ̂_k < N_k ⟹ p_k ≤ α ρ̂_k` --- then the algorithm it
builds belongs to the aRTS family (`IsARTS`). This reduces verifying `IsARTS` for a concrete design
to the pure arithmetic of its throttle inequality (`probVecKernel_apply_singleton` identifies the
policy mass on arm `k` with `p n h k`). -/
@[specifies aRTSAlgorithmOfProb "the packaging is faithful: the algorithm's policy assigns arm `k` \
exactly the mass `p n h k`, so a throttle proved for the probability vector holds verbatim for the \
algorithm"]
lemma aRTSAlgorithmOfProb_isARTS (p : (n : ℕ) → Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n → 𝓐 → ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ n a, Measurable fun h ↦ p n h a) (hnn : ∀ n h a, 0 ≤ p n h a)
    (hsum : ∀ n h, ∑ a, p n h a = 1) (θ₀ : 𝓐 → ℝ) (T : (𝓐 → ℝ) → 𝓐 → ℝ) (α : ℝ)
    (hthrottle : ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n) (k : 𝓐),
      (n : ℝ) * histTarget θ₀ T k n h < (pullCount' n h k : ℝ) →
        p n h k ≤ α * histTarget θ₀ T k n h) :
    IsARTS (aRTSAlgorithmOfProb p hp hnn hsum) θ₀ T α
proof:
where
  throttle n h k hover := by
    rw [show (aRTSAlgorithmOfProb p hp hnn hsum).policy n
        = probVecKernel (fun x : Hist Unit 𝓐 ℝ n × Unit ↦ p n x.1)
          (fun a ↦ (hp n a).comp measurable_fst) from rfl,
      probVecKernel_apply_singleton _ _ (h, ()) k (hnn n h k)]
    exact hthrottle n h k hover

specifies.comment: the packaging is faithful: the algorithm's policy assigns arm `k` exactly the mass `p n h k`, so a throttle proved for the probability vector holds verbatim for the algorithm
